pick.name: PostHog Cloud
pick.what: Analytics, replay, flags, experiments, surveys, errors, LLM analytics
pick.why: Largest free bundle; one SDK covers 5 tools; EU or US cloud; MIT core self-hostable
pick.free_limits: Monthly free: 1M events, 5k recordings, 1M flag requests, 100k exceptions, 1,500 survey responses (per search of pricing page; fetch truncated); 1 project on free; billing caps per product
pick.license: posthog-js npm: Apache-2.0 AND MIT; PostHog server MIT (ee/ separate)

alts.name: Mixpanel Free
alts.why: Strongest pure analytics UI; 1M events + 10k replays
alts.free_limits: 1M events/mo, 10k replays, unlimited seats, 5 saved reports/seat; Growth starts at $0 with per-event billing above 1M

alts.name: Umami (self-host)
alts.why: If you only need traffic + custom events
alts.free_limits: Self-host free; Cloud Hobby 100k events, 1 site, 6-month retention

candidates.name: PostHog
candidates.verdict: PICK; pricing says >90% of companies use it free

candidates.name: Mixpanel
candidates.verdict: Alt: better funnels UI, fewer extra tools

decision: PostHog replaces analytics, replay, flags, surveys and backup error tracking with one SDK and generous free quotas. Never send PHI to it for healthcare clients; use self-host or strip properties.

verify.note: posthog.com/pricing is JS-rendered (fetch and curl return no allowances). The figures match PostHog's long-standing published allowances but are not primary-confirmed here. posthog-js 1.441.0 (2026-10-28) confirmed; npm licence field is 'Apache-2.0 AND MIT', not plain MIT.
